title: Contain a bad run before it becomes a platform incident
description: Inject drift, a concurrent writer, or an apply failure. Then change refresh behavior, state locking, and the state boundary to see what the workflow can detect or contain.

incidents.label: Out-of-band drift
incidents.summary: An operator changes a managed network rule outside Terraform.
incidents.operatorQuestion: Will the plan compare state with the remote object before proposing reconciliation?
incidents.recovery: Review a normal or refresh-only plan, decide whether configuration or the remote object is authoritative, then reconcile deliberately.

incidents.label: Concurrent apply
incidents.summary: Run B starts while Run A holds the same state and is applying changes.
incidents.operatorQuestion: Can a second writer operate against the same state snapshot?
incidents.recovery: Let the supported backend lock serialize writers. Investigate a stale lock before using force-unlock with its lock ID.

incidents.label: Apply fails midway
incidents.summary: The provider returns an error after earlier graph nodes completed successfully.
incidents.operatorQuestion: Which successful changes are recorded, and what must be replanned?
incidents.recovery: Resolve the cause, inspect state and remote objects, then create a fresh plan. Terraform does not automatically roll back a partial apply.

stateScopes.label: One platform state
stateScopes.detail: Network, data, identity, and application resources share one state and lock.

stateScopes.label: One state per domain
stateScopes.detail: The selected application domain owns its graph and consumes narrow outputs from platform domains.

stateScopes.label: One state per service
stateScopes.detail: A small service graph is isolated, with more cross-state interfaces to operate.

executionPolicies.label: Normal saved plan
executionPolicies.detail: Refresh remote objects, save the reviewed plan, and apply that artifact.

executionPolicies.label: Speculative plan, then apply
executionPolicies.detail: Review an unsaved plan, then let apply generate a new plan.

executionPolicies.label: Saved plan with -refresh=false
executionPolicies.detail: Skip remote reads and plan from cached state. This can miss external changes.

fixtureNote: Resource and owner counts describe this teaching fixture only. They are not Terraform performance benchmarks or universal state-size limits.
